F1.caption: The static weighted sum. Left: on six thousand opposed cases, the hardest conflict type, a Hartian validation rule contradicts itself on 100% of them, certifying both outcomes at once; the weighted sum never contradicts itself, deciding about 52% at tau = 0.2 and reporting the rest as unresolved. Thirty-seed means. The sum's coherence holds as an entailment; the rule's 100% is the rate on cases built to be directly opposed, and on unstructured draws it is 45.4%; the determinacy rate is measured throughout. See Section IV.D. Right: net legal force on three worked examples, the sign giving the verdict. TVA v. Hill returns +1.205 under Burger and -0.285 under Powell, opposite determinate verdicts on one statute, and Obergefell returns +0.295.

F2.caption: Practice is not unitary. Each column is one mechanism's emergent weight structure across the nine principles; darker cells carry more weight. All four mechanisms clear the four requirements of Part III. Uptake concentrates on the textual and structural principles and drives the four moral principles to zero; reliance and appointment lift the moral principles highest; strategic lifts the structural principles highest. Reliance and appointment converge (rank correlation +0.93 between the mean weight vectors), so the four dynamics realize three distinct structures, not four. Appointment is the marginal mechanism on noise tolerance, clearing it on twenty-six of thirty seeds. The heavier moral tier under reliance and appointment is partly a category-size effect: the moral tier holds four principles to the structural tier's three and the textual tier's two, so under correlated activations it accrues broader aggregate force.

F3.caption: The determinacy threshold is a choice the theory does not make. A case counts as determinate when the size of its net force exceeds the threshold tau. Raising tau lowers the share of cases decided smoothly and monotonically for every mechanism plotted, from 1.000 at tau = 0 to between 0.794 and 0.828 at tau = 0.30, with no kink, no plateau, and no privileged value anywhere on the curve; 0.20 is a common default and is marked for reference, where the stipulated engine decides 86.2% of cases. The curve has a closed form in tau, which the simulation matches to a maximum error of 0.0106. Berman's text permits an aggregative system to eschew thresholds altogether, so the faithful baseline is the bare sign of net force, the tau = 0 end of this figure, where determinacy is at its maximum. Curves are thirty-seed means for the stipulated engine of Part IV and for the uptake, reliance, and strategic mechanisms of Part VI; the appointment mechanism's weights come from a separate simulation this sweep does not rebuild. All four requirements of Part III hold across the whole range for each of the three emergent mechanisms plotted.

F4.caption: What the threshold governs. A global sensitivity analysis apportions the variance in each output among four inputs varied together: the threshold, the weights' dispersion, the correlation among activations, and the share of principles carrying no weight. Left: for whether a case is decided at all, the threshold dominates, taking a total-order variance share of 0.849 (95% confidence interval 0.827 to 0.871), against 0.156 for activation correlation, 0.023 for sparsity, and 0.008 for weight dispersion. Right: for the substantive requirements the ordering reverses. On the margin over the hierarchical Hart the threshold's first-order share is 0.176 against activation correlation's 0.810, and on the magnitude probe 0.020 against 0.919. The left panel reports total-order shares, which include each input's interactions with the others; the right panel reports first-order shares from a smaller run and should be read as a ranking rather than as precise shares. The threshold governs how much law comes out determinate. It does not govern whether the model's substantive properties hold.

F5.caption: Only cardinal aggregation reads how strongly a principle applies. Under a magnitude-only perturbation, which holds every sign and every within-case rank fixed and changes only the strengths, the four cardinal rules change their verdicts on 2.3% to 7.5% of cases; the weighted sum sits at 4.96% with its determinacy gate at tau = 0.2 and at 2.3% on the bare sign of net force. Every ordinal rule changes its verdict on exactly none of them (0.000, by construction, having never read a magnitude), and the lexical foils on effectively none (lexicographic 0.24%, cascade 0.000). The measurement separates the cardinal family from the other six rules by roughly a factor of ten at its narrowest. It does not separate the ordinal rival from the lexical foil, which sit together at or within rounding of zero; that division is conceptual, not one this instrument reports.

theorems_table.caption: The five results, and the scope each is proved under. Two hold on any activation distribution whatever. One divides: the weighted sum never contradicts itself on any case, while a validation rule contradicts itself whenever at least two principles apply strongly each way, which is a condition on the case. One holds for the reliance mechanism only, since under uptake a principle's weight simply is its invocation frequency. One holds under independent activations and does not carry over to correlated ones. The right-hand column reports what the simulation adds rather than what establishes the result.
